cohort: The study included 364 singleton pregnancies (266 individuals) with IBD and 45,048 singleton pregnancies (32,189 individuals) without IBD delivered between 1998 and 2016.
finding: While inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) was not associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy overall, it was linked to an increased risk of pre-eclampsia, preterm delivery, and small for gestational age birth weight.
mod_finding: IBD was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
